option.counterfactual: Every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of S² × S² with finitely many fixed points has at least four, even when the fixed points are degenerate.
option.approach: Establish the upper bound of four using independent rotations of the two spheres, then concentrate on excluding three by spectral-invariant or quantum-product arguments.

judge.reason: It claims that the minimum is four, which is the same claim as e2.

options.counterfactual: Four is not the minimum: a Hamiltonian with exactly three distinct fixed points exists.
options.approach: Audit the explicit ball-replacement construction supplied by the other teams, focusing on its global coordinate neighborhood and smooth collar matching. If those steps hold, combine the resulting three-critical-point function with a small-period exclusion argument.

options.approach: Seek a precise version of the degenerate Arnold cup-length theorem applicable to this monotone product. Verify its minimal-Chern-number hypothesis before using it to exclude one or two fixed points.

options.approach: Examine whether the claimed coordinates around the entire joining arc actually exist with the prescribed endpoint normal forms. A framing incompatibility would explain why locally valid formulas do not define the asserted global replacement.

options.counterfactual: The claimed universal lower bound of four is correct, but the proposed three-critical-point construction fails at a global gluing step despite satisfying all its local differential identities.

options.counterfactual: The cup-length lower bound does not apply here, and a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with only one or two isolated fixed points is possible.
options.approach: Compute the quantum product relations for the two sphere classes and examine what spectral-invariant inequalities they imply. Determine whether those relations still force at least three distinct action carriers without invoking a general cup-length theorem.
